sources.doc: MakeMyTrip ICICI Bank Signature Credit Card T&C
sources.quote: earn rates per Rs 200: domestic 1.25, international 1.50, flights 2.00, hotels/holidays 4.00 My Cash

examples.title: Rs 8,000 domestic spend outside MakeMyTrip
examples.why: 1.25 My Cash per Rs 200: 40 x 1.25 = 50. 1 My Cash = Rs 1 on MakeMyTrip.

examples.title: Rs 1,000 domestic spend: My Cash rounded to nearest integer (down)
examples.why: 1000/200 x 1.25 = 6.25; My Cash on each qualifying transaction is rounded off to the nearest integer at posting -> 6.

examples.title: Rs 1,100 domestic spend: My Cash rounded to nearest integer (up)
examples.why: 1100/200 x 1.25 = 6.875 -> nearest integer 7 (a floor-per-block rule would give 6).

examples.title: Rs 8,000 international spend
examples.why: 1.5 My Cash per Rs 200 on international spends outside MakeMyTrip: 40 x 1.5 = 60.
examples.not_checkable_reason: Needs an international flag or the booking type (flight vs hotel) on a single merchant with no MCC; C3.1 context cannot carry it (D14a, D13c).

examples.title: Rs 20,000 flight booked on MakeMyTrip (booking_type flight)
examples.why: 2 My Cash per Rs 200 on flights booked on MakeMyTrip: 100 x 2 = 200. The rule depends on booking type, which a merchant name alone does not give.
examples.not_checkable_reason: Needs an international flag or the booking type (flight vs hotel) on a single merchant with no MCC; C3.1 context cannot carry it (D14a, D13c).

examples.title: Rs 20,000 hotel booked on MakeMyTrip (booking_type hotel)
examples.why: 4 My Cash per Rs 200 on hotel and holiday bookings: 100 x 4 = 400.
examples.not_checkable_reason: Needs an international flag or the booking type (flight vs hotel) on a single merchant with no MCC; C3.1 context cannot carry it (D14a, D13c).

examples.title: Rs 3,000 fuel
examples.why: Fuel transactions are non-qualifying on the Visa Signature card (the fuel exception in the MITC is only for the Amex network variant of MakeMyTrip/HPCL Coral cards).

examples.title: Rs 10,000 EMI purchase
examples.why: EMI, balance transfer and personal loan on credit card transactions do not earn My Cash.

examples.title: Rs 1,00,000 insurance premium with 900 of the 1,000 points already earned this card year
examples.why: Base would be 500 x 1.25 = 625, but insurance reward points are capped at 1,000 per anniversary year (MITC); only 100 remain.

examples.title: Rs 20,000 insurance premium after the 1,000-point annual limit
examples.why: Insurance points beyond 1,000 per anniversary year are not given.

research_notes.issuer_says: MITC: for the MakeMyTrip ICICI Bank Credit Card, insurance reward points are capped at 1,000 per anniversary year.

research_notes.cardpipeline_says: rounding_mode round on block 200, 1.25 points per block
research_notes.issuer_says: T&C: My Cash for each qualifying spend transaction is rounded off to the nearest integer at posting (final points, not per block). My Cash is modelled as a points unit (base_points_per_block 1.25), so accrual_rounding = points_half_up is correct; cashback_rounding is not used.

research_notes.cardpipeline_says: two rules on platform MakeMyTrip by booking_type
research_notes.issuer_says: Rates are per booking type (flights 2, hotels/holidays 4 My Cash per Rs 200). Merchant-only context cannot distinguish them; keep as separate rules and do not collapse to an up-to rate. Trains/buses/cabs rates are not stated in this T&C. The two MakeMyTrip booking-type rules are set to info (flag depends_on_txn_attribute).
A separate newer ICICI MakeMyTrip programme (changes dated 10 Nov 2026, 6 and 3 My Cash per Rs 100, round down) is a different product from the Signature card page used here. Not applied.
MITC says e-wallet reload earns nothing for ICICI cards (Amazon Pay excepted). Utility and grocery caps in the general MITC table do not list this card.
The cap override has no target rules in the source; the whole-array reward_rules override adds an insurance rule (mmt-insurance-base) that carries cap_reference so the cap is not card-wide.

research_notes.cardpipeline_says: international-retail and base-domestic-retail carry geography/platform restrictions
research_notes.issuer_says: Issuer: 1.5 My Cash per Rs 200 international, 1.25 domestic outside MakeMyTrip. International is info (no international flag in context); the base domestic rule is kept unrestricted so it is not lost.

research_notes.item: base rule also covers international spend (Phase 1 approximation)
research_notes.issuer_says: The domestic base 1.25 per Rs 200 is made unrestricted (channel_type all) because the international 1.5 accelerator is info in Phase 1; international spend therefore earns 1.25 in the engine instead of 1.5 (under-states, never over-states).
Fuel, wallet and EMI exclusions are rewritten to MCC / rail so they are real exclusion rules; fees/interest are not purchases and remain info.
